Scythe. The worker-placement and asymmetric game designed by Jamey Stegmaier and released in 2016, set in an alternate-history nineteen-twenties Europe dominated by mecha, enormous mechanical walkers, where players control different factions competing for resources, territory, and military supremacy.

Five asymmetric factions—Saxony, Crimea, Polania, Rusviet, and Nordic—begin in different board positions with unique special abilities, mechanical abilities, and economic bonuses, ensuring divergent viable strategies. Worker-placement actions include Move, Gain Resources, Build, Produce, Trade, and Bolster, taken in turn order. Turn order is dynamic and can be purchased, adding resource-conversion strategy.

Victory requires a mix of territorial control, factory presence, power tokens, and resource conversion into power. This balanced scoring system prevents dominant strategies. The game incorporates a threat system. Military aggression is penalized by opponent power increases, incentivizing diplomacy over conflict despite military presence.

The game is acclaimed for world-building and art direction. The steampunk alternate-history setting is integrated thematically without overwhelming mechanics. It features stunning artwork by Jake Parker and highly asymmetric faction powers with dynamic gameplay that rewards different strategic approaches.

Numerous expansions introduce new factions, modules, and mechanics. Windcrossed, All Creatures, and the Modular Board expand the base game. A successor title, Scythe: New Division, was released in 2021, exploring different factions in the same universe.
